feedback: Reject: the shape applies to every nltl:frame and its generic upper end, but TRF-046 applies to the strengthened upper end of a main frame and an intermediate ice frame. Constrain applicability to those declared frame types and encode the strengthened-part relationship with nltl:hasStrengthenedPart before enforcing the upper-end attachment. Preserve the eligible alternatives: a deck structure, top or bottom tank boundary plating, or an ice stringer. Do not add the at-or-above-ice-belt condition as an unconditional attachment requirement; it qualifies only the separate permission branches.

Preserve the prior applicability, hasStrengthenedPart, and eligible-supporting-structure instructions. The candidate still omits the separately stated permission branches required by the non-empty COMPLETE comparisonModel: represent termination above a supporting structure, the at-or-above-ice-belt condition, ordinary frame scantlings for the part above it, and, for an intermediate frame, the horizontal connection member linked to the adjacent main frame with the same scantlings as the main frame. These must be conditional permissions, not unconditional attachment requirements, and must use their declared owners and paths.

Preserve the prior applicability, hasStrengthenedPart, eligible-attachment alternatives, and conditional-permission instructions. Repair the owner/path structure: nltl:hasUpperEnd has required owner frame (and canonical domain transverseFrame), but the candidate places it on frameStrengthenedPart nodes. Constrain the upper end from each applicable frame branch, while retaining ordinaryFrameScantlingsUsed on the strengthened part; move or rewrite the permission queries to traverse the frame's strengthened part and upper-end paths. Also bind the supporting structure used for hasTerminationAboveSupportingStructure to the eligible structure attached by hasAttachedSupportingStructure, so a different arbitrary supporting structure cannot satisfy the at-or-above-ice-belt permission condition.

Preserve the applicability, owner/path structure, eligible attachment alternatives, and binding of the terminating support to the attached supporting structure. Repair the permission logic: the regulation says the ordinary non-ice-strengthened scantlings and the intermediate-frame horizontal connection are permitted, not mandatory. Do not reject a qualifying frame merely because ordinaryFrameScantlingsUsed is absent or false, and do not require every qualifying intermediate frame to have a horizontal connection member. Instead, conditionally validate any claimed permission: when ordinaryFrameScantlingsUsed is true, require the frame end to terminate above the attached eligible deck/stringer and that supporting structure to have supportingStructureAtOrAboveIceBeltUpperLimit true; when a horizontal connection member is represented for an intermediate frame, require it to connect to the adjacent main frame and have sameScantlingsAsMainFrame true, under the same qualifying termination condition. Keep ordinaryFrameScantlingsUsed on the strengthened part and the connection properties on their declared owners.
